chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, who said: Abu Abdullah al-Razi narrated to me, from Ali ibn Suleiman ibn Rashid, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Isma'il ibn Kathir ibn Basam, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said:
The thieves are three: the one who withholds the alms-tax, the one who considers it permissible to devour the dowry of women, and likewise the one who borrows a debt and does not intend to repay it.

key_terms.مُسْتَحِلُّ مَهْرِ النِّسَاءِ: One who considers it permissible to devour women's dowry

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of thieves according to Imam al-Sadiq in al-Khisal?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) expanding the metaphorical concept of 'theft' beyond physical appropriation to include financial negligence and injustice. This classification highlights how withholding *Zakat*, consuming *Mahr* unjustly, and borrowing with intent to default are treated as equivalent to stealing property, emphasizing the sanctity of wealth in Shia jurisprudence. The hadith serves as a critical link between ritual obligations and commercial ethics, warning that intent (*niyyah*) can transform a legal transaction into a form of theft.
